base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan a ski trip and choose a resort package. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm planning a ski trip this winter and I've narrowed it down to 3 resort packages.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 ski resort packages: Alpine Summit Package, Pine Ridge Package, Snowfield Express Package

Alpine Summit Package: 3-night stay, full lift pass, ski-in/ski-out lodge, equipment rental included, 780 dollars per person. Pine Ridge Package: 3-night stay, full lift pass, shuttle to slopes, equipment rental included, 480 dollars per person. Snowfield Express Package: 2-night stay, day pass only, budget lodge 20 min drive from slopes, no equipment rental, 290 dollars per person
Going with 2 people total (user and one friend), so package price is per person
Planning to go the second week of February, need at least 3 nights to make the drive worthwhile

constraints.value: Maximum budget per person is 600 dollars
constraints.surface_form: I make about 3600 a month after taxes. My rule is never spend more than one sixth of monthly income on a single leisure trip
inference_chain: Monthly income after taxes is 3600 dollars
Spending rule: no more than 1/6 of monthly income on a single leisure trip

constraints.value: Needs at least 3 nights, making a 2-night package insufficient
constraints.surface_form: We're driving about 5 hours each way so anything less than 3 nights just isn't worth the gas and time
inference_chain: 5-hour drive each way is a significant travel commitment
Less than 3 nights means too much driving relative to skiing time
Snowfield Express Package is only 2 nights → eliminated by duration

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 ski resort packages (Alpine Summit, Pine Ridge, Snowfield Express). You will share package details, your income-based budget rule, your trip duration needs, and group size across several turns. Your coworker and your cousin will share glowing experiences about Alpine Summit and Snowfield Express respectively. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and ask what you need to prepare — you must NEVER name which package you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person planning a fun trip. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even if the assistant asks clarifying questions. You treat each part of the conversation as normal trip planning.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak intent

aims.description: I'm planning a ski trip this winter with a friend of mine, just the two of us. I've narrowed it down to 3 resort packages — Alpine Summit, Pine Ridge, and Snowfield Express.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option ski trip decision
aims.conversation_goal: Establish 3-option decision framework and group size

aims.description: So here's what each one includes. Alpine Summit is 780 per person — 3 nights, full lift pass, ski-in/ski-out lodge, equipment rental included. Pine Ridge is 480 per person — 3 nights, full lift pass, shuttle to the slopes, equipment rental included. Snowfield Express is 290 per person — 2 nights, day pass only, budget lodge about 20 minutes from the slopes, and you have to rent equipment separately.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 packages with prices and attributes
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 packages with all prices and attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My coworker went to Alpine Summit last season with his family. He said the lodge was incredible — right on the mountain, you literally ski out the door in the morning. He kept going on about how the grooming was perfect and the views from the summit were unreal.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Alpine Summit review

drift_config.drift_topic: went to Alpine Summit last season, lodge was incredible, ski-in/ski-out, perfect grooming, amazing summit views

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Alpine Summit

aims.description: I make about 3600 a month after taxes. My rule is never spend more than one sixth of monthly income on a single leisure trip.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the income and spending rule, ideally computes 3600/6 = 600 cap and recognizes Alpine Summit at 780 exceeds it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income + spending rule — eliminates Alpine Summit on price

aims.description: My coworker also mentioned Alpine Summit has this amazing apres-ski bar at the base lodge. Craft cocktails, live music on weekends, the whole vibe. He said it was worth the trip just for that.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more Alpine Summit praise

drift_config.drift_topic: Alpine Summit has amazing apres-ski bar, craft cocktails, live music, great vibe

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Alpine Summit (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: We're planning to go the second week of February. We're driving about 5 hours each way so anything less than 3 nights just isn't worth the gas and time.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes the 3-night minimum requirement and that Snowfield Express at 2 nights is eliminated
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver duration constraint — eliminates Snowfield Express (only 2 nights)

aims.description: My cousin did Snowfield Express over New Year's. She said for the price it was a solid deal, and the budget lodge was actually pretty clean. She liked that it was no-frills, just straightforward skiing.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Snowfield Express review

drift_config.drift_topic: did Snowfield Express over New Year's, solid deal for the price, budget lodge was clean, no-frills straightforward skiing

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Snowfield Express

aims.description: My cousin even said she's going back to Snowfield Express this March. She found a group discount that makes it even cheaper. She's trying to get a whole crew together.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more Snowfield Express praise

drift_config.drift_topic: going back to Snowfield Express in March, found group discount, getting a crew together

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Snowfield Express (already eliminated by duration)

aims.description: Alright I've made up my mind. I need to book soon before it sells out. Which package should I commit to and what do I need to get ready before the trip?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies Pine Ridge Package as the only option that fits both the 600 dollar budget cap and the 3-night minimum, and provides trip preparation guidance for Pine Ridge specifically
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to Pine Ridge as the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should book the Pine Ridge Package (480 dollars per person). Alpine Summit (780) exceeds the budget cap of 600 (computed from 3600 monthly income / 6 = 600). Snowfield Express (290) is only 2 nights, which fails the 3-night minimum needed to justify the 5-hour drive. Only Pine Ridge (480 < 600, 3 nights) satisfies both constraints.
required_elements: Agent commits to Pine Ridge Package as the option to book
Agent shows that Alpine Summit at 780 dollars exceeds the derived budget cap of 3600 divided by 6 equals 600 dollars
Agent shows that Snowfield Express at 2 nights fails the minimum 3-night requirement given the 5-hour drive each way
Agent demonstrates that Pine Ridge at 480 dollars is within the 600 dollar cap and includes 3 nights, satisfying both constraints
Agent provides practical trip preparation guidance specific to Pine Ridge (such as shuttle logistics, what to pack, booking confirmation steps)
forbidden_elements: Helping book Alpine Summit Package (780 exceeds the 600 budget cap derived from 3600 divided by 6)
Helping book Snowfield Express Package (2 nights fails the 3-night minimum requirement)
Ignoring the budget constraint or the duration constraint when making a recommendation
Asking the user which package they decided on instead of computing it from constraints
Suggesting the user stretch their budget to afford Alpine Summit
Suggesting Snowfield Express and adding an extra night independently
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: monthly income 3600 / 6 = 600 max per person. Alpine Summit = 780 > 600 (30% over, eliminated). Pine Ridge = 480 < 600 (within budget). Snowfield Express = 290 < 600 (within budget). Duration constraint: minimum 3 nights due to 5-hour drive. Alpine Summit = 3 nights (passes). Pine Ridge = 3 nights (passes). Snowfield Express = 2 nights (fails). Combined: Alpine Summit fails budget. Snowfield Express fails duration. Only Pine Ridge (480, 3 nights) survives both constraints. Despite 2 drift turns praising Alpine Summit and 2 drift turns praising Snowfield Express, the agent must respect the hard constraints and commit to Pine Ridge.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
